A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeshMosaic with the same authors, core method, and experimental foundation. Text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A.1–A.2 are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on three datasets, a 27-participant user study, and appendix ablations, runtime measurements, and generation examples.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds the qualitative comparison in Figure 2, including commercial Hunyuan3D.

M1.justification: Both versions use BFS-ordered patch generation, GRU boundary conditioning, global/local point-cloud features, local quantization, and displacement-based patch assembly. V2 clarifies adjacency, ordering, and boundary handling, but does not establish a changed algorithm or architecture.

E1.justification: Training sources and ShapeNet, Thingi10K, and Objaverse evaluation coverage are retained. Unsegmented inputs, alternative segmentations, and CLAY-based text/image examples already appear in v1. Figure 2 adds comparisons on an existing character example without introducing a distinct task or domain.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 2 adds commercial Hunyuan3D, labeled Scaled-BPT, alongside BPT, DeepMesh, and MeshMosaic. The four comparators in the quantitative evaluation and user study—MeshAnythingV2, BPT, TreeMeshGPT, and DeepMesh—remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same dataset sample counts, metrics, training settings, user-study procedure, and ablation regimes. V2 newly identifies BPT as the released 0.5B model and clarifies existing segmentation choices; these disclosures do not establish revised settings. The added visual comparison specifies no distinct new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 2 adds a focused qualitative case study of geometric completeness on a complex character, highlighting missing geometry in comparison outputs and including Hunyuan3D. Appendix A.2 retains the same conditioning ablations, segmentation comparisons, detail-recovery analysis, runtime analysis, and diversity examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed-based variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the performance comparisons. The user-study aggregation and other statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 2 adds qualitative outputs and findings concerning reconstruction quality and geometric completeness relative to BPT, DeepMesh, and Hunyuan3D. Every numerical entry in Tables 1–3 is unchanged. The relocated gallery and reformatted detail-recovery figure retain their existing results.

T1.justification: The patch-count formula and Appendix A.1 point-to-face ratio remain unchanged. V2's tokenization and BFS explanations do not introduce a substantive mathematical derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the claims about scalable generation beyond 100K triangles, fidelity, and user preference. V2's introduction adds the specific claim that its 0.5B model achieves comparable visual fidelity and better geometric completeness than commercial Hunyuan3D.

C2.justification: V2 adds rationales for GRU conditioning and stable boundary gluing, and explains that the existing aircraft ablation deliberately uses random cuts to expose seams. It also explains Hunyuan3D's exclusion from batch evaluation. The symmetry and long-runtime limitations remain; future work shifts toward synchronous generation and speed.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies patch adjacency and coordinate-based BFS tie-breaking, default PartField inference partitioning without an explicit patch-count cap, and the BPT-0.5B comparator. It clarifies the existing aircraft ablation's random segmentation. Hardware, training duration, learning rates, preprocessing, and project access remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds the Hunyuan3D Studio reference and positions MeshMosaic against its commercial BPT-derived model. The new Preliminaries section elaborates existing DeepMesh and Meshtron foundations. The broader related-work coverage is retained; citation-style changes do not add research content.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a Preliminaries section, expands selected method explanations, moves the conclusion after limitations, and makes localized wording and heading edits. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The manuscript changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, substantially resizing and repositioning displays. V2 adds comparison and tokenizer figures, redraws the architecture diagram, and expands the boundary illustration with a 2D example. The gallery and face-count histogram move into the appendix; the fighter-jet comparison becomes unnumbered.

improvement.justification: The new background section, clearer method diagrams, and explicit ordering and segmentation details address modest explanation and reproducibility gaps in v1 while preserving its quantitative and appendix evidence. The commercial comparison adds context, but remains qualitative; its smaller-model claim is not established because Hunyuan3D's size is undisclosed. Overall, the documentation gains support a limited improvement rather than stronger empirical validation.
